title: Remove the 34 ms of per-request generation recomputation
harness: /tmp/u9root scratch checkout; the branch's own drop-launcher (cargo build --release) invoked directly with BL_CHECKOUT_PLATFORM and the preparation lock held so the client reuses the pinned SDK; warm realm; /tmp/u9/one.bl = (println 1).

measurement.note: the first warm service run pays the resident's first full computation; the median is the steady state. Phase marks: service query 340 us, local computation 26.2 ms (BL_CHECKOUT_PHASE_TIMES=1).

design.authority: a per-tree resident (`drop-launcher --generation-service ROOT`) that holds all three tokens and watches the engine tree, the project tree and the extra roots with inotify
safety: the tokens are computed by the same checkout_generations() the client uses, so a cached answer and a local one are byte-identical (unit test)
every answer drains the kernel event queue immediately before replying; any event invalidates the affected scope and it is RECOMPUTED, never guessed
watches are installed before a computation; an event during it makes the answer a fallback
IN_Q_OVERFLOW, a failed watch (ENOSPC), a replaced root (dev+ino change), or a non-local filesystem (statfs magic) all yield `fallback`, and the client computes locally
the realm remains the authority for retirement: it stores BL_CHECKOUT_SOURCE_GENERATION and retires when the token it receives differs
design.scopes: engine, runtime and project; a manifest append under .bl/ is project-only, everything else keeps the watch's mask (over-invalidation costs one recomputation, under-invalidation could serve a stale token)

cargo_test_branch.note: the two failures are builder_tests::build_custody_reports_io_errors_and_releases_after_publication_failure and builder_tests::failed_metadata_prevents_real_native_publication_even_with_a_guessed_library, both also failing on main (124 passed, 2 failed) where native preparation needs store/artifact custody this sandbox lacks

gate.helper_edit_scenario: old, then new function, then both: green

real_checkout.root: /tmp/u10real, a scratch copy of main (reverted main), engine+project trees only: .git (2.5G), research (5.4G) and .local (21G) are not engine or project inputs and were excluded; every policy root, test/ and env.bl are the real bytes

cold_first_answer.note: the resident's first computation; the client falls back for that one request (it starts the resident after its own local compute)

reverted_bug.symptoms: every request paid the 150 ms read timeout then fell back; residents accepted connections and never answered; two residents for one socket; 'Resource temporarily unavailable' afterwards
causes: the watch plan recursed the WHOLE checkout root: on a real tree (research/, .git, generated trees) the first answer took seconds, past every client timeout

a manifest `D` line names a directory to watch, but the code watched its PARENT — a recorded search root under /tmp made /tmp watched, so unrelated temp traffic (including the service's own debug log in /tmp) invalidated the project pin on every answer, an endless dirty loop
no single-instance lock: concurrent clients could each start a resident; the loser left an orphan and the socket path was not replaceable deterministically
debug logs were written under a directory the service could watch, feeding the loop
fixes: bounded watch plan: the engine policy's roots (nix/engine-inputs.json) recursively, the checkout root non-recursively, the project root non-recursively, declared/extra roots and overrides/ recursively, and manifest entries (D: the directory, L: its parent); hard cap 20,000 watches
recorded inputs that no longer exist are not watched through a shared ancestor: they are stat'd once per answer, so their appearance invalidates the project pin without /tmp noise
one resident per root: an advisory flock on <socket>.lock; the winner unlinks any stale socket and binds; losers exit 0
debug logs live beside the socket in the runtime dir, never in a watched tree; expected startup misses are not reported as declines
